- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment volatility is high (frequent +/–0.50 changes) and news volume is low, model underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 10–15 days.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is >10% above model, check if sentiment was bullish 3–5 days prior — if yes, model likely overfitted; apply 2–4% downward bias.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and news volume is high, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- When sentiment change is negative and price is rising, model often misreads trend — reduce forecast by 1–2% for 5–10 days.
- For 30d forecasts, if model is consistently below true outcome by 2–4%, check if sentiment was bullish 1–2 days prior — if yes, model is underestimating sentiment-driven momentum.
